items.title: 68642_Jo Jones oral history interview
items.q: Until Mr. Joe DiMaggio came in and the man, Mr. Edison, Marie Cramer's brother, liked Joe DiMaggio, baseball players did not stay in reputable hotels.

ctx.x: In one particular portion of the United States?

No particular. I had the advantage of being on these carnivals and circuses and what-have-you, you know, and the show break up. You don't know what's happening. I do remember that we were connected with peoples that had foreign intrigue. These peoples - Hungarians, Lithuanians and what-have-you, trapeze artists and what-have-you - they taught us how to eat, they taught us how to think, they taught us everything, they taught us personal hygiene, they taught us everything, you see. And like I said, you had to be a…

You're a musician? What? You're with a carnival? Out! You know how difficult it was for us to stay and it had nothing to do with color. It was just you were identified. with a semi-pro team, Oh, you're a baseball player? I don't care what you was playing with. I don't care if you was a major leaguer. All the antics of Ty Cobb and people; everybody knows what those people were or what Babe Ruth did. Well, they were big stars; they could get away with things. But a kid today - he'd look like Little Lord Fauntleroy…
